items.title: RT by @charliebilello: RT by @charliebilello: US National Debt has increased by $715 billion since July 1 while the 10-Year Treasury yield has jumped from 4.48% to 4.75%. Washington’s solution? Increase buybacks of longer-dated Treasuries to $4 billion. But swapping longer-maturity debt for shorter-maturity debt doesn’t solve the underlying problem: we’re still borrowing at an alarming pace. Until that changes, the upward pressure on rates will remain. Video:
items.content:
US National Debt has increased by $715 billion since July 1 while the 10-Year Treasury yield has jumped from 4.48% to 4.75%.

Washington’s solution?

Increase buybacks of longer-dated Treasuries to $4 billion.

But swapping longer-maturity debt for shorter-maturity debt doesn’t solve the underlying problem: we’re still borrowing at an alarming pace.

Until that changes, the upward pressure on rates will remain.

Video:  youtube.com/watch?v=9M5N3lQG… 
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Sep 1, 2026

Instead, we would get soaring inflation and a collapsing dollar. Printing money can raise GDP in dollars. It can’t create prosperity.
items.content:
"We could have GDP of 14, 15, 16, and 20." - President Trump today

We could...

If we printed trillions of dollars and dropped them from helicopters.

That would certainly boost nominal GDP.

But real GDP? Not so much.

Instead, we would get soaring inflation and a collapsing dollar.

Printing money can raise GDP in dollars. It can’t create prosperity.
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Sep 1, 2026

items.title: RT by @charliebilello: RT by @charliebilello: The best we can say in studying past military conflicts: with the passage of time, the stock market has tended to rise - and the more time that has passed, the more it has risen. Why? 2 reasons: 1) all wars eventually come to an end, and 2) the economy & earnings, even if impaired in the short run, still tended to grow in the long run despite these conflicts.
items.content:
The best we can say in studying past military conflicts: with the passage of time, the stock market has tended to rise - and the more time that has passed, the more it has risen.

Why?

2 reasons: 1) all wars eventually come to an end, and 2) the economy & earnings, even if impaired in the short run, still tended to grow in the long run despite these conflicts.
— Charlie Bilello (@charliebilello) Aug 31, 2026
